what: In the area clustered at the panel center (normal distribution, mean .5, standard deviation 1/6), 0 to 2 1px rings appear per frame and grow from 0 → 1× over 4 seconds (radius = panel short side × .1), and it fades out past 70%. The rings come in two layers — the back layer dark gray, the front layer light gray, and the front layer is drawn only inside a mask silhouette so a face emerges within the cluster of rings. Pressing the panel puts one light ring at that spot. It runs only while visible on screen (PixiJS)

options.rate: Max number of rings spawned per overlap in a frame (0~rate evenly), default 2
options.life: Time for one ring to grow (seconds), default 4
options.size: Final radius once fully grown — share of the plate’s short side, default .1
options.fade: Progress at which fading begins (0~1), default .7
options.mask: face (default — our mask silhouette) · none (front layer also covers the whole panel) · part (child [data-fx-part=mask] the image’s alpha as the silhouette)
options.--fx-ring-bg · --fx-ring-dim · --fx-ring: Background, back layer and front layer colors, default --kf-bg · text color 32% · 66% mix
options.delay: Wait before the first ring (seconds), default 0. Brand uses .95 (the original canvas appears after the framework wakes up, leaving about 1s of empty background after the first paint)

from.where: index.html .ok-hero__canvas (hero — original: PixiJS 6.0.0, gsap.ticker drives the pixi ticker, each tick every layer gets a ring at randInt(0,2), scale 0→1 over 4s linear, alpha 1→0 after 70%, background #080d1b · rings #555555 · inside mask #aaaaaa, pressing gives #aaaaaa rings)

note: The original mask image (a mask-face png) is not used — it is replaced with our own shape: an egg-shaped face with eye and mouth holes and a beard tuft. The ring color is mixed from the skin color, so it leans slightly toward the background compared to the original’s neutral gray. Pressing does not block page scroll.
